# Two instances of one component must not name one node twice.
#
# Splicing a body copies every `#id` in it into the caller. The callee's state
# is renamed per instance and its ids were not, so both counters below carried
# `#out`, and whichever element the backend resolved first answered for both --
# bumping either one updated the same text.
#
# The first occurrence keeps the name: with a single instance, which is the
# common case, `#out` is unambiguous and a test naming it means that one. The
# later instance is the one that gives up the name, because the program has no
# way to say which of the two it meant.

sngl generate --lang=none --platform=html --out=out app.sngl
exists out/index.html

# No write goes to a name the page never declared: both instances' updaters
# reach the element each was emitted as.
! grep 'out\.textContent' out/index.html
! grep 'out__1\.textContent' out/index.html

# Two state slots, two elements, and each handler writes only its own.
grep '\$0.textContent = String\(state.n__inst0\)' out/index.html
grep '\$1.textContent = String\(state.n__inst1\)' out/index.html
! grep '\$0.textContent = String\(state.n__inst1\)' out/index.html
! grep '\$1.textContent = String\(state.n__inst0\)' out/index.html

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import app "sngl:app"

component counter ui {
    var n = 0
    button(text="+", @click { n += 1 })
    text #out(value=string(n))
}

component main ui {
    counter()
    counter()
}

app.window {
    main
}
